_derivation: Derived from the corpus, not invented. Frequencies are exact counts over ALL
823,142 archived messages (628,342 with text, 194,800 media-only), not a sample.
Two categories were DISCOVERED by reading the unmatched pile rather than assumed:
stock_news  — company-specific news (order wins, stake changes, policy). The
single largest thing a first-pass regex missed.
fragment    — 33.9% of texted messages are <=20 chars: captions, reactions,
emoji. Separated from `unknown` so escalation is not swamped.
29.8% of texted messages still match NO hand-written rule at an average of 102
characters. That is the architectural case for an LLM router: a rules engine
cannot classify a third of substantive traffic.

confidence_threshold._note: Provisional. P6 calibrates this against the P3 holdout. Below it, the message goes to the Importance Assessor rather than being routed on a guess.

ipo_new.description: A new IPO announced, RHP/DRHP filed, dates and price band published
ipo_new._note: Rarest high-value category and the most concentrated in tier1 (82%), which independently validates the tiering. IPO World leads the folder by a median 12.3h on these.

ipo_allotment.description: Allotment status out, allotment odds, subscription figures
ipo_allotment._note: Time-critical: allotment windows close. Overrides quiet hours.

ipo_gmp.description: Grey market premium figure or GMP table
ipo_gmp.threshold_rule: notify when GMP >= 10% of the upper price band, or when it moves >= 5 percentage points from the last notified value for that IPO
ipo_gmp._note: Do not notify every GMP tick — they move daily. plan/04-decision-rules.md Gate 3 uses the 10% floor. Cross-check against a second channel before quoting: IPO World once posted LCC at 73 when trackers showed a high of 50.

ipo_listing.description: Listing today, listed at, listing gain

regulatory.description: SEBI / RBI / exchange rule or policy change
regulatory._note: Rare and always material. Longest average message in the corpus (438 chars) — these are substantive.

stock_news.description: Company-specific news: order wins, stake changes, management commentary, sector policy
stock_news._note: DISCOVERED category — the largest miss of the first-pass regex. Needs a materiality check: most is minor.

results.description: Quarterly results, profit, revenue, dividend announcements

market_news.description: Index/macro: Nifty, Sensex, market open/close, breaking macro

institutional._note: Daily rhythm, low individual value, useful as a daily roll-up.

trade_call.description: A buy/sell recommendation with entry, target or stop-loss
required_context: source channel and its tier from tiers.json
whether a stop-loss was given — ranged 70% to 1% across channels and is the strongest quality marker
the channel's promo ratio when high
standing footnote that these are third-party calls, not verified
trade_call._note: DELIVERED, like every other intent. These are the user's own messages going to their own inbox; the system adds context, it does not withhold categories. Extract symbol/direction/entry/target/stop-loss so per-channel accuracy can be measured over time.

performance.description: Self-reported win claims: 'done of the day', '5/6 hit', 'no SL hit today'
performance._note: Marketing, not information — unauditable by construction. 42% of it originates in the `useless` tier, which validates that tiering. Logged with a reason, never silently dropped.

promotional.description: Join our channel, paid/premium group, referral, coupon, DM me

greeting.description: Good morning, welcome, thanks, festival greetings

fragment.description: <=20 characters with no signal: captions, reactions, emoji, single words
fragment._note: The single largest bucket. Separated from `unknown` deliberately: escalating 213k fragments would bury the escalation path in noise it cannot act on. A fragment attached to MEDIA is not discarded — it goes to the vision path, because the content is in the image.

unknown.description: Substantive text that fits no other category
unknown._note: NEVER discarded. 29.8% of texted messages at an average of 102 characters — far too large and too substantive to drop. This is the category that makes an LLM router necessary rather than a rules engine.

escalation._rule: The two-stage decision that makes 'never miss anything' real.
escalation.stage_1: Is this promotional, performance-marketing, greeting, or a bare fragment? -> discard, LOGGED WITH A REASON. Never silent.
escalation.stage_2: Not droppable, and the router's confidence is below threshold -> hand to the Importance Assessor, which asks one question: would a retail investor want to know this today? If yes -> notify, flagged UNCLASSIFIED.
escalation.invariant: A message is NEVER dropped without a recorded decision and reason. Wrongly emailing the user is a minor cost; silently swallowing a material alert is the failure this system exists to prevent.
escalation.media_rule: A message with media and little or no text is NOT a fragment — the content is in the image. Route to vision, then re-classify on the extracted text.

delivery_actions.notify: email immediately, subject to rate limit and quiet hours
delivery_actions.notify_on_threshold: email only when the category's threshold_rule fires
delivery_actions.assess_importance: Importance Assessor decides, then email as UNCLASSIFIED
delivery_actions.digest: hold and roll into the daily digest
delivery_actions.discard: do not email; write the event and the reason to content.agent_events
